articles.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
articles.description: Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.
articles.author: Russell Brandom

articles.title: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
articles.description: A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a U.S. military contract worth almost $50 million.
articles.author: Tim Fernholz

articles.title: Honeyjar offers AI tools to improve PR and comms at every company
articles.description: Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken. But could AI actually make things better?
articles.author: Anthony Ha

articles.title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
articles.description: Microsoft president Brad Smith calls for urgent AI regulation, saying milk and washing machines have more oversight than AI companies.
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan

articles.title: This AI startup says it can generate permit-ready blueprints in minutes
articles.description: Blueprints AI, a bootstrapped startup based in Santa Monica, developed software that produces code-compliant construction blueprints from a photo, PDF, or sketch.
articles.author: Kirsten Korosec

articles.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 starts tomorrow: Your final chance to secure up to $100 ticket savings
articles.description: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 starts at 8 a.m. PT on Oct. 13 for three days of insight, tech discovery, and connections. Save up to $100 before doors open.
articles.author: TechCrunch Events

articles.title: Former Plaud exec raises $26M for AI app that listens to you in the background
articles.description: One of the core promises of AI is that the more it knows about a person, the better it will be able to assist them with tasks and make appropriate suggestions, which, if you'll believe the tech companies, requires apps and devices to listen, watch, or record users' activity all the time and gather all possible context.
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
